Direct evidence: abstract pp. 0-1 says 707 minimally perturbed claim-counterclaim pairs and stage-specific ranking/generation metrics; the introduction (PDF lines 84-107) explains stance replacement and that the scientific domain was selected for objective factual grounding and clearer isolation.

findings.claim_support: direct_full_text for study identity, pair design, and stage-specific evaluation; abstract-level for summarized result that bias can occur at different stages and be amplified. Do not extend the reported result to software architecture work.
findings.task_applicability: adequately mapped as a feasible evaluation prompt/discriminator; benefit to repository architecture research remains untested.
findings.feasible_discriminator: On matched repository questions, compare the existing scout report with a variant requiring a concise counterclaim whose stance is minimally changed. Score contrary evidence found, source support, viable alternatives, and reviewer correction/time. If retrieval traces are unavailable, score source coverage separately from final synthesis.
gaps_and_limits: The benchmark is scientific claim verification with stance-flipped factual claims, not architectural exploration or Luna subagents.
The source does not validate prompt-injection boundaries, direct expert inspection, independent patch acceptance, or review timing.
Peer-review status is not explicitly verified in this run.

primary_source.title: RepoCoder: Repository-Level Code Completion Through Iterative Retrieval and Generation
primary_source.identity_status: Official ACL Anthology EMNLP 2023 record and proceedings PDF identity verified.
primary_source.peer_review_status: Proceedings publication verified; review process not explicitly checked in this bounded verification.
primary_source.content_status: Full text opened. PDF lines 122-141 say later retrieval uses the previous prediction; Table 2 (PDF lines 360-374) shows third-round EM above round one for GPT-3.5-Turbo and CodeGen-Mono-350M on line completion, with fourth-round scores falling from round three in both.

findings.claim_support: direct_full_text for iterative prediction-conditioned retrieval and cited table values. The report's specific example that the first query missed an API signature was not independently confirmed by the excerpt returned in this verification and is excluded from the accepted claim.
findings.task_applicability: adequately mapped as a proposed matched test; completion results do not establish improved architecture research or mixed-model handoff.
findings.feasible_discriminator: Compare ordinary repository mapping with one candidate-hypothesis-conditioned lookup of the artifact that could discriminate it; score independently verified novel alternatives, source accuracy, omissions, reviewer correction, and time.
gaps_and_limits: RepoCoder evaluates code completion, not open-ended research, alternative discovery, or architecture decisions.
Observed round gains are small and not monotonic; the fourth round does not uniformly improve over the third.
Do not treat generated architectural explanations as reliable retrieval queries without the proposed matched test.

primary_source.title: CodeRAG: Finding Relevant and Necessary Knowledge for Retrieval-Augmented Repository-Level Code Completion
primary_source.identity_status: Official ACL Anthology EMNLP 2025 record and proceedings PDF identity verified.
primary_source.peer_review_status: Proceedings publication verified; review process not explicitly checked in this bounded verification.
primary_source.content_status: Full text opened. Abstract and methods (PDF lines 118-163) establish code-completion scope, multi-path code retrieval, and reranking; benchmark context (lines 517-571) confirms tested code-model sizes and ReccEval/CCEval. The detailed path definitions and snippet-count ablation were not independently verified in the returned excerpts.

findings.claim_support: direct_full_text for code-completion scope and multi-path retrieval as a method; unresolved for specific sparse/dense/dataflow roles, gains from adding paths, and the 1-to-3 versus 5-to-10 snippet-retention comparison.
findings.task_applicability: unresolved for the full compound contribution; a limited complementary-code-route experiment is plausible, but pruning and architecture-workflow benefit remain unverified.
findings.feasible_discriminator: A matched repository study can classify accepted evidence by route and test whether distinct code routes surface contrary facts; separately measure reviewer rework and retrieval time. Test pruning only if source verification confirms the reported ablation.
gaps_and_limits: CodeRAG is specialized repository code completion, not smaller reasoning-model research or architecture selection.
The full report's suggestion to include semantic documentation or issue context is an extrapolation, not a route evaluated by CodeRAG.
The paper itself reports reranker/retriever-model misalignment may remain (PDF lines 786-792).
The verification open cap was exceeded, so the detailed evidence-route and pruning subclaims remain unresolved here.
